reviewerSummary: RFI 26-001 (CalVCB Compensation and Restitution System Modernization) is due 2026-09-24, 2:00 PM Pacific, submitted electronically to ITAcquisitions@victims.ca.gov as the completed Attachment 1 worksheet only — no cover letter, appendices, or supplemental materials, 10 pages max, single-spaced, 12-point font, one-inch margins. Note: this due date appears to have already passed relative to today; check Cal eProcure for an amendment, extension, or successor solicitation before submitting [GAP-001 | DataBillity | Confirm current RFI status/amendments on Cal eProcure]. Fit is largely Partial-to-Gap on direct government past performance and unverified on core company facts: DataBillity's founding date, size, socioeconomic status, platform architecture, and any prior government implementations are not yet confirmed in the grounding facts, so Part I and several Part II/IV answers are placeholder-heavy. No confirmed partners are named in the facts, so all coverage is shown as DataBillity-direct or Gap. High-priority open items: (1) verify RFI is still live, (2) supply company background/size/founding year, (3) confirm platform architecture (home-grown vs. based on another platform) and any government references, (4) resolve the page-limit/cover-letter ambiguity per Att. 3 Q49 vs §1.F before drafting final copy, (5) decide whether to answer the nine-item upgrade/enhancement/configuration classification table, which requires product-specific detail not yet supplied. Several answers rely on the issuer's own unresolved ambiguities (page limit scope, external user counts, DOJ/court integrations, data cleansing cost treatment) — these are logged as questions to the issuer, not gaps in our response. Decisions needed from DataBillity leadership: whether to pursue, what cost figures (if any) to disclose as non-binding ROM, and who owns the signed certification in Part I.
strategicNotes: This RFI is explicitly market research shaping a future Cal eProcure solicitation, with invite-only demonstrations anticipated October 2026 (R61) — logged as a High Prime gap since registration/demonstration mechanics are not yet confirmed [see GAP list]. The RFI shows no stated preference among COTS, MOTS, integrated product set, COTS Configurable, or custom (R41), and no incumbent is named in the facts, so this does not read as pre-written for a specific competitor; the strongest competitive lever will be configurability without custom code (directly answering the root-cause theme in R42) and a clean government-references narrative. Because grounding facts contain no confirmed DataBillity government past performance, the single biggest risk to a competitive response is Part I credibility — if no qualifying reference exists, teaming with a partner that holds direct state/local government claims or benefits-system implementation experience would materially strengthen Parts I, II, and VI; no such partner is currently confirmed, so this is noted as a teaming option rather than a commitment. Recommend closing the platform-lineage, security-framework, and hosting-model gaps (GAP-003, GAP-018, GAP-019) early, since these recur across Parts II, III, and IV and gate several other answers. The cost model (Part V) cannot be populated at all without DataBillity-supplied pricing; treat this as a hard blocker for a compliant submission, not a nice-to-have.
questions: Does the 10-page limit in Attachment 1 include the worksheet's own question text, Part I company information, and the signature block, or only the respondent's answers?

Section 1.F references written responses including the Attachment 1 worksheet, while Att. 3 Q49 prohibits supplemental appendices or attachments; may respondents include a brief cover letter, and does it count toward the 10-page limit?
For Q48, should data cleansing and remediation be included in the base cost estimate or presented as an optional/separate line item?
Are exchanges with the Department of Justice, crime-reporting agencies, and courts in scope as required system integrations?
Is the external online application service intended to be replaced by the new solution, or integrated with it going forward?
Beyond the 350-400 internal, JP, and CRC users, how many external users (claimants, providers, advocates, court personnel) should respondents assume for capacity and licensing?

sections.title: Company Information and Experience
sections.body: DataBillity (Billity AI) responds to RFI 26-001 as Prime, with company background, size, and founding details to be confirmed prior to submission. [GAP-002 | DataBillity | Confirm company founding date, headcount, and corporate history for Part I background question]. Our proposed solution's technical foundation — whether built natively by DataBillity or based on licensed/partner platform components — is not yet documented in the grounding facts and must be confirmed before we can accurately answer whether the platform is home-grown or built on another organization's base. [GAP-003 | DataBillity | Confirm whether the Billity AI platform is home-grown or built on a third-party/partner platform, and document the technical lineage]. Regarding government experience: the grounding facts contain no confirmed prior implementations with government agencies, department names, or specific applications delivered. Rather than assert unverified past performance, we flag this as an open item: if DataBillity or a partner has relevant state or local government claims, benefits, or compensation-system experience, that reference detail (agency name, system implemented, dates, scale) must be supplied before submission. [GAP-004 | DataBillity | Provide specific government agency references, systems implemented, and dates, or confirm none exist and adjust the response accordingly]. Administrative identifiers required for a compliant Part I submission — UEI, CAGE code, business size determination, and any socioeneconomic certifications (e.g., small business, disadvantaged business enterprise) — are not present in the grounding facts and cannot be fabricated. [GAP-005 | DataBillity | Supply UEI, CAGE code (if applicable for state work), business size, and socioeconomic status certifications]. Applicable NAICS code(s) for this engagement (e.g., custom computer programming services or computer systems design) must also be confirmed by DataBillity rather than assumed. [GAP-006 | DataBillity | Confirm applicable NAICS code(s) for this response]. The signed certification required in Part I per §1.F/Att. 1 must be executed by an authorized DataBillity representative prior to submission. [GAP-007 | DataBillity | Identify authorized signatory and execute Part I certification]. No confirmed subcontractor or teaming partner is named in the grounding facts for this response; if a partner is added to close a capability gap (e.g., prior state-government claims-system implementation), that partner's name, address, identifiers, size/socioeconomic status, NAICS, contract vehicles, and point of contact would need to be added here as its own administrative block. [GAP-008 | DataBillity | Decide whether a teaming partner is needed to strengthen government past-performance references, and if so supply that partner's administrative data].

sections.title: Solution
sections.body: Our proposed solution is intended to directly address the ten challenge items CalVCB names (§1.D), particularly the lack of agility in functionality changes (item 1), the absence of an adjustments module (item 2), no appeals workflow (item 3), no correspondence engine (item 4), and no attribute-level audit trail (item 9), by offering configurable workflows, rules, letters, and reports that can be changed without custom coding, consistent with the target end state CalVCB describes (R31, R53). Specific configuration mechanisms, rules-engine architecture, and out-of-the-box module names for Billity AI are not detailed in the grounding facts, so we cannot yet state precisely which named modules map to which challenge item. [GAP-009 | DataBillity | Provide product/module names and confirm mapping to each of the 10 challenge items, including adjustments, appeals, correspondence, and audit trail modules]. On the off-the-shelf vs. configured vs. customized question (R105, R63), our typical approach is to lead with configuration over custom code wherever the platform supports it, since CalVCB's stated problem is coding-dependent change (R42); the specific balance of COTS, configuration, and any custom work for CalVCB's nine sample changes cannot be stated without confirmed platform capability detail. [GAP-010 | DataBillity | Classify Billity AI's typical configuration-vs-customization split for claims/eligibility/correspondence functionality]. On scalability and flexibility for future security, accessibility, and compliance needs (R104, R17), our typical approach is to design for evolving standards rather than point-in-time compliance, but specific mechanisms (e.g., role-based access control extensibility, accessibility conformance level such as WCAG, and how the platform absorbs new NIST/FISMA/SAM control updates) require confirmation. [GAP-011 | DataBillity | Confirm platform's accessibility conformance standard and mechanism for absorbing new security/compliance requirements over time]. We note the RFI leaves the underlying solution-approach decision open — COTS, MOTS, integrated product set, COTS Configurable, or custom (R41) — and recommend CalVCB weigh total cost of ownership and long-term agility, not just initial fit, given the challenge theme of change being coding-dependent (R42).

sections.title: Integration (Inputs and Outputs)
sections.body: CalVCB's target end state requires integration at minimum with the existing Bill Review Service, the State Controller's Office, the Franchise Tax Board, EDD, and TotalAgility (R53), and the solution must at minimum support the existing bill-adjudication interface, with integrated adjudication considered as an option (R54). Our typical approach to input/output capability is to expose standard integration methods (e.g., API-based and file-based exchange) appropriate to each named system, but the specific interface protocols, data formats, and connection methods Billity AI supports for these five named integrations are not yet confirmed. [GAP-012 | DataBillity | Confirm supported integration methods (API, SFTP, batch, etc.) for Bill Review Service, SCO, FTB, EDD, and TotalAgility]. The RFI's own Q&A leaves open whether exchanges with the Department of Justice, crime-reporting agencies, and courts are in scope as required integrations, since the narrative describes them as part of eligibility determination but the Q&A integration list omits them (R96); we recommend CalVCB clarify this before a future solicitation, and we would size our integration approach accordingly once confirmed. Similarly, whether the external online application service is meant to be replaced or integrated going forward is unresolved in the RFI text (R97); our typical approach supports either path — replacing the external intake with a native, integrated online application (closing challenge item 6, R10) or integrating with the existing external service — but the correct target must be confirmed. [GAP-013 | DataBillity | Confirm with CalVCB (or state assumption) whether external online application intake is to be replaced or integrated, and adjust integration scope accordingly]. Migration inputs are scoped to active claims plus full history and supporting documents from CaRes, explicitly excluding external databases (R58, R33); our typical data migration approach and specific ETL tooling for this scale are addressed in Part IV.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Implementation methodology: our typical approach to a modernization of this type begins with a business-understanding phase to document current-state workflows across the ten named challenge items (R5-R14) before configuration begins, given CalVCB's stated need to move from coding-dependent change to configurable, agile workflows (R4, R42). A specific phased implementation timeline for CalVCB, and examples of comparable implementations completed within the last 5 years, cannot be provided from the grounding facts as supplied. [GAP-014 | DataBillity | Provide implementation timeline methodology and specific examples of implementations completed in the last 5 years, per Att. 1 Part IV]. User acceptance testing: our typical UAT approach is to test each configured workflow against the business rules it was configured to enforce, with CalVCB business users validating outcomes before go-live; role-specific UAT scenarios for the 350-400 HQ, JP, and CRC users (R30) would need to be scoped jointly with CalVCB once business processes are documented. Data validation and migration: our typical approach is to validate source data completeness and integrity against CaRes records before migrating active claims with full history and documents (R33, R76), excluding external databases per the stated scope (R58); the specific migration tooling and data-quality remediation approach for CalVCB's data are not yet confirmed. [GAP-015 | DataBillity | Confirm data migration tooling and specific data validation/cleansing methodology for CaRes data]. Whether data migration is included in the base cost or billed separately is addressed in Part V, noting the RFI's own Q48 answer does not clarify treatment of data cleansing costs (R95) — we recommend CalVCB clarify this before a future solicitation. Upgrades, enhancements, and configuration changes: our solution's definitions of system/platform upgrade versus enhancement versus configuration change, our release cadence, and our classification of the nine sample changes CalVCB will provide, are not yet established for this response. [GAP-016 | DataBillity | Define upgrade vs. enhancement vs. configuration change for Billity AI, state upgrade/enhancement release cadence, and classify the nine sample functional items requested in Att. 1 Part IV]. IT technical and functional support: our typical approach separates technical support (platform availability, defect resolution) from functional support (business-rule and configuration assistance to CalVCB staff), but specific service-level commitments, support tiers, and staffing model for CalVCB are not yet defined. [GAP-017 | DataBillity | Define technical and functional support approach, including support tiers and typical response times]. Security and compliance: CalVCB requires alignment with NIST 800-53, FISMA, and SAM 5300, with no CJIS or IRS 1075 requirement (R56), and any GenAI use must follow SIMM 5305-F and SAM 5300 (R57). Whether Billity AI currently maps its controls to NIST 800-53/FISMA/SAM 5300, and whether any GenAI features are part of the proposed solution, must be confirmed rather than assumed. [GAP-018 | DataBillity | Confirm current security control framework alignment (NIST 800-53, FISMA, SAM 5300) and whether GenAI features are part of the proposed solution, with SIMM 5305-F governance if so]. Hosting: State data center, CDT-approved cloud, or a vendor's California-compliant cloud are all acceptable to CalVCB (R55); our typical approach supports multiple hosting models, but which model(s) Billity AI can support for a California state government workload is not yet confirmed. [GAP-019 | DataBillity | Confirm which hosting model(s) — state data center, CDT-approved cloud, vendor California-compliant cloud — Billity AI can support].

sections.title: Costing Model
sections.body: CalVCB has explicitly stated that no budget, funding range, or implementation timeline has been established (R59, R90), and requests a non-binding cost model broken down by one-time vs. recurring cost, module, and phase, with sizing assumptions stated (R60, R72). No cost figures, rate cards, or pricing models for DataBillity/Billity AI are present in the grounding facts, so we cannot provide a rough order of magnitude at this time; any cost figures included in the final response must come from DataBillity's actual pricing and be explicitly labeled non-binding, for planning purposes only, per §1.F. [GAP-020 | DataBillity | Supply cost model inputs (implementation, product/license, maintenance, support, training) broken out by one-time vs. recurring, module, and phase, sized against the 350-400 role-based user count in R30] Whether data migration and data cleansing/remediation costs are included in the base estimate or shown as a separate line item is itself unresolved in the RFI's own Q&A (R95); we recommend stating both options with the assumption made explicit. We would size any cost model against the population figures CalVCB has published — noting the RFI's own Q&A points respondents to the CalVCB Annual Report for record counts, claim/bill/payment volumes, and historical data years rather than supplying them directly (R88). [GAP-021 | DataBillity | Pull record counts, claim/bill/payment volumes, and historical data years from the CalVCB Annual Report to ground the cost model's sizing assumptions].

sections.title: Evaluation
sections.body:
Recommendations for the future solicitation: First, we recommend CalVCB resolve, before releasing a formal solicitation, the open questions its own Q&A leaves unanswered — particularly the solution-approach preference among COTS, MOTS, integrated product set, COTS Configurable, or custom (R41), and phased vs. single cutover vs. broader business transformation scope (R41, R86) — since these materially change vendor cost models and implementation risk. Second, we recommend CalVCB publish, ahead of the solicitation, the external online application's future disposition (replace vs. integrate, R97), the DOJ/court/crime-reporting integration scope (R96), external user volumes for licensing (R98), and demonstration success criteria (R91), since each of these currently requires a vendor assumption that could otherwise be inconsistent across responses. Third, given the challenge theme of manual, coding-dependent change driving the named consequences — higher call/escalation volume, inconsistent information across divisions, and increased time to approval and payment (R46-R52) — we recommend the future solicitation weight configurability and low-code change management heavily in evaluation criteria, not just initial functional fit. Fourth, we recommend CalVCB clarify the Attachment 1 page-limit scope (whether it includes worksheet question text and Part I company information, R93) and reconcile the apparent conflict between §1.F's reference to written responses and Att. 3 Q49's prohibition on supplemental attachments (R94), so vendors are not penalized inconsistently for formatting choices. Additional requirements CalVCB should consider adding to the future solicitation: multilingual correspondence beyond English/Spanish given the stated gap (R8, R45, R89), attribute-level audit trail and automated separation-of-duties as explicit, testable requirements (R9, R13, R34, R44) rather than narrative description, and a defined records-renaming capability so uploaded documents do not require re-upload to correct a filename error (R11).

[GAP-001 | DataBillity | The stated RFI due date (2026-09-24) appears to be in the future relative to typical processing but should be verified against Cal eProcure for amendments, extensions, or a superseding solicitation before submission.]
